escalation_routing.note: Elapsed time changes routing only, never truth, evidence, or authority. FYIs remain dashboard-only and are not escalations.

authority_tiers.principle: A P-level is decision authority and nothing else. It is not seniority, not capability, not a queue position, and never an input to model or effort selection — decision 0006 forbids selection by rank. Two rules keep the ladder honest: authority is per action rather than per level, so holding a tier grants only the actions that tier names; and independence inverts the ladder, because a P3 verdict binds P0 and P1 alike and is cleared only by a recorded waiver from the role the QA contract names.

levels.label: Owner
cannot: overrule an independent QA verdict without a recorded waiver named in qa.json

levels.label: Deputy — IT Manager III, Integration and Delivery
holds: the wake target for every technical escalation
cannot: main, release, tag, publication or Pages

levels.label: Standing coordination
holds: portfolio, dependency, WIP and capacity visibility
completion councils and Gate D convening

levels.label: Independent verification
holds: the exact-head verdict, which no tier may overrule
WITHHOLD that blocks promotion at any level
levels.note: Ranked below P2 in decision authority and above every tier in verdict finality. That is deliberate: independence comes from a non-maker reviewer at an immutable head, not from position.

levels.label: Delivery seats
cannot: claiming an overlapping path or ref
push, PR, merge, deploy or release
changing product behaviour to clear a blocker

rules.not_a_capability_ladder: A P-level never selects a model or an effort; decision 0006's risk-and-station matrix does that, and a tier named after a role is rejected.
rules.authority_is_per_action: Holding a tier grants only the actions that tier enumerates. Authority for one action implies authority for none of the others.
rules.independence_binds_upward: A P3 verdict binds every tier including P0. It is cleared only by the waiver authority qa.json names for that risk class, recorded with its reason.
rules.escalation_follows_the_tree: A tier is not a routing table. Escalation follows escalation_parent and the classes in escalation.json; only owner-exclusive classes reach P0.
rules.namespace_is_reserved: P<n> is shared with incident and defect priority. The subject disambiguates: a code on a team or actor is authority, a code on an issue, ticket or directive is priority. The contract must keep saying so.

authority_tiers.namespace_note: P<n> carries two meanings in this project, separated by SUBJECT, per the owner: on a team or an actor it is AUTHORITY (this ladder); on an issue, ticket or directive it is PRIORITY (P0 most urgent). 'P1 Help Desk lead' is an authority statement; 'P1 WITHHOLD' and 'incident-p0' are priority. Nothing infers one from the other, and neither reading is ever applied to a subject of the other kind.

disambiguation.rule: The subject decides the meaning. A P-code attached to a team or an actor is authority; a P-code attached to an issue, ticket, directive or defect is priority.
disambiguation.never: Read a priority code as authority, or an authority code as priority, because the two share a letter.
disambiguation.known_ambiguous_artifact: The recovered 2026-08-28 census carries rows such as 'P0 IT Manager III', where a priority code and an actor name sit adjacent in rendered output. Those rows are historical PRIORITY rows and predate this rule. They are evidence, not authority statements, and docs/reconstruction/team-evidence/ labels each one accordingly.
